content.text:
I improved `0.html` with three changes. I haven't seen it in a browser yet (more on that below).

- **Page height (`0.html:13`):** I replaced `width: 100vw; height: 100vh` with `min-height: 100dvh`. On phones, `100vh` is measured as if the browser toolbars were hidden. When they're showing, the page is taller than the screen, so it scrolls a little and the circle sits below center. `dvh` uses the part of the screen you can actually see. `width: 100vw` wasn't needed because the body is already full width.
- **Circle size (`0.html:19-20`):** I changed the fixed `400px` to `min(400px, 100dvmin)`. 400px is wider than most phones (about 360–390px) and taller than most phones held sideways, so part of the circle got cut off. Now it stays 400px when there's room and shrinks to fit when there isn't.
- **Screen readers (`0.html:25`):** I added `role="img" aria-label="Black circle"`. The circle is the only thing on the page, but screen readers had no name to read out for it. If the piece has a real name, use that as the label instead.

I left the title and the id `ae683f770` as they are, since they look like a generated identifier.

I wanted to check the page at a few window sizes, but my command to look for an installed browser needed approval. This session can't give approval, so the command was blocked. To check it yourself, open the page and make the window narrower than 400px: the circle should shrink instead of getting cut off.
